# Ida Ashdown

## Overview

- **Age:** Young child, around nine or ten years old  <sub>[v5 c4 P7](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0007), [v5 c4 P26](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0026)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v5 c4 P7](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0007), [v5 c5 P3](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0003)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolgirl  <sub>[v5 c5 P3](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0003)</sub>

## Appearance

Ida has a delicate face with slanted, deep-blue eyes carrying a hint of longing and sadness. Her limp, pitch-black hair is worn in braids without curls, and her lips frequently part above tiny ivory teeth. She has small, pale hands that sometimes become cold or rough.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P7](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0007), [v5 c18 P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005), [v5 c28 P26](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0026)_

## Personality

Ida is a quiet, sensitive, and deeply romantic young girl who harbors a tender grief over the death of her mother. Intensely shy and sensitive to the opinions of others, she often feels a sense of shame regarding her family's neglected household and lack of domestic training. Despite her fearful and modest nature, she possesses profound courage and self-sacrifice when motivated by her desire to protect others or bring happiness to her father.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P7](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0007), [v5 c4 P26](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0026), [v5 c5 P3](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0003), [v5 c9 P10](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0010), [v5 c9 P11](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0011), [v5 c33 P36](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0036), [v5 c34 P0](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0000)_

## History

Ida Ashdown spent her childhood in Glen St. Agnes following the death of her mother, Cecilia. Raised alongside her siblings Grace, Tobias, and Rupert by their absent-minded father and elderly Aunt Martha, she cherished warm memories of her mother while coping with a dusty home, poor food, and worn clothing. Desiring to improve her family's circumstances, she occasionally tried to clean the manse or mend her father's clothes. When the orphan Mary Stubbs took shelter in Mr. Taylor's barn, Ida showed compassion, housing her at the manse and taking the brave step of visiting Miss Winifred Kerr to persuade her to adopt Mary. She frequently read her mother's old cookbooks to cope with meager meals and envied other children who had mothers, music lessons, or new accessories. Driven by warnings from Mary Stubbs, she developed a deep terror of stepmothers, fearing a second marriage would alienate her father from his children. Despite her fears, after overhearing her father weeping in despair over his love for Clementine Ainslie, Ida conquered her terror and walked to the Ainslie house to beg Clementine to marry her father for his happiness. Her courageous intervention resolved the misunderstanding between Clementine and Rev. Ashdown, paving the way for their engagement.
